subject: Physics
basis: Every ruling names the section that teaches it and was checked against the
book TEXT via generated-papers/physics-corpus.json, not against section
titles. A title match is not evidence: JEE's Transformers has no heading in
the State Board AC chapter, yet the topic is taught in full one chapter
earlier, and a title-only pass would have called it a gap.
Coverage is judged on what the exam DEMANDS, not on how our bank happens to
solve it. Absent rulings are absent on purpose - an unreviewed subtopic has
no row at all, so 'not yet assessed' stays distinguishable from 'covered'.

stateBoard.note: 13.5 derives the voltage-current relation for R, L and C individually; reactance appears 66 times in the chapter.

ncert.note: NOT in NCERT at all: 'LC oscillation' occurs ZERO times across all four Physics volumes, both years - the rationalised edition dropped it. The State Board still teaches it at 13.7, so this is a gap on the NCERT side, the reverse of the usual direction.

stateBoard.note: Series LCR in 13.5, resonance in 13.8 and sharpness/Q-factor in 13.9.

Taught in ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION (12.15), not the AC chapter - a teacher looking under AC Circuits will not find it. Treatment is complete: turn ratio Ns/Np (eq 12.49), ideal-transformer power relation (12.50), and both step-up and step-down cases.
The State Board names it the Geiger-Marsden experiment (15.3) before Rutherford's model (15.4).

Neither book teaches X-ray SPECTRA: 'characteristic X-ray', 'Moseley' and 'X-ray spectrum' are ZERO across both corpora. The State Board's only X-ray material is XI:13.3.6, which places X-rays on the EM spectrum - that is not this subtopic.

ncert.note: Same: zero occurrences across all four NCERT Physics volumes.

stateBoard.note: 13.6 teaches the concept - carrier wave, and amplitude/frequency/phase modulation - but MODULATION INDEX is absent from the corpus, and JEE's questions here lean on it.

ncert.note: NCERT dropped Communication Systems entirely; 'modulation' survives only as 2 incidental mentions in XII ch8 EM Waves.

stateBoard.note: Ground, space and sky-wave propagation are taught, with antennas and the ionosphere; the antenna-height/range relation is absent.

ncert.note: Zero 'ground wave' / 'space wave' / 'sky wave' anywhere in NCERT Physics - the chapter was removed.

stateBoard.note: SPLIT ACROSS YEARS: resistor combinations in Std XI, Kirchhoff's laws and the Wheatstone bridge in Std XII.

No taught transient section in either book. 'time constant' occurs twice in the State Board corpus and both are incidental asides inside other topics (e.g. displacement current in XII:8), never a growth/decay treatment.

ncert.note: Likewise incidental only; NCERT teaches no RC or LR transient section.

stateBoard.note: CROSS-YEAR: the State Board teaches EM waves in Std XI, where NCERT places them in Std XII.
